key_findings.value: The highest degree of short-range ordering (highest x-ray scattering intensity) was observed at 250 °C; the 250 °C/14 day anneal gives the maximum ordering state. (Ordering studied in a separate study, refs [16,20].)

unmapped_findings: The highest degree of short-range ordering (characterised by x-ray scattering intensity) was observed at 250 °C for isochronal annealings of Fe-18%Al for 14 days; the activation energy for this ordering reaction was found to be only 0.3 eV/atom and 100 h were sufficient at 250 °C for reaching a near-equilibrium state (SRO study reported in separate refs [16,20]).
Quenching from 1100 °C suppressed short-range ordering nearly completely, giving the minimum-ordering state.

Short-range ordering in the studied Fe-Al alloys, controlled by heat treatments below 600 °C, has no major impact on the deformation behaviour; only heat treatments above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys.
The 250 °C/14 day anneal produces the maximum degree of ordering but gives the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal, i.e. short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness.
No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320 °C (a different heat treatment than the 250 °C/14 d state of this sample).
